data.title: Brazilian assets steady as investors gear up for pivotal elections
data.description:
Key points:
  • Brazilian assets steady ahead of Sunday election
  • Colombia peso up over 1%, government cuts spending budget
  • Venezuelans call for elections in first national protest in nearly two years
  • Mexican economy exceeds expectations in August

By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Johann M Cherian

Brazilian assets were steady on Friday as investors geared up for a presidential election in Latin America's largest economy that will determine the trajectory of the country for the next four years.

Voters will decide between right-wing candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday. Bolsonaro had performed better than expected earlier in the month, but recent polls have shown his lead over Lula was narrowing, sparking volatility in local markets.

The real has rallied 2.6% this month, marking its biggest monthly gain since April, while local stocks have advanced 9.5%, its strongest month since January, on expectations that the senator would adopt fiscal consolidation policies if he won. However, analysts said he was yet to offer clarity on the subject.

On Friday, the currency hovered at 5 to the dollar, while stocks were little changed. International bonds (105756CN8=), (105756BY5=) were marginally higher.

Ahead of the vote, data showed consumer inflation rose less-than-expected in the month to mid-October.

"Brazil is at the verge of fiscal dominance dynamics, and anything that improves the fiscal situation can lower risk premia," said Alejandro Cuadrado, managing director, global head FX & LatAm Strategy at BBVA.

"Lower risk premia implies the central bank can find more room to cut, lower interest rates, imply better valuations for Brazilian equities and potential growth and that brings flows from the offshore into Brazil."

MSCI's index tracking regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) and currencies (.MILA00000CUS) were flat as investors weighed the repercussions of higher oil prices on the global economy.

Brent crude prices rose 2% to their highest since early May after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

Oil exporter Colombia's peso appreciated the most among regional currencies, up 1% near a one-month high.

The currency has been buoyed recently by remarks by the local central bank on the likelihood that interest rates could stay higher for longer in an effort to combat inflation. The peso is one of the best performing in Latam, up 20% for the year.

Public finances were also in focus as the country's government cut this year's spending budget by 13.8 trillion pesos ($4.33 billion), although it was smaller than previously announced.

The Mexican peso inched up 0.2% against the dollar, but eyed its seventh straight week of losses, hit by expectations of a narrowing of the US-Mexico interest rate differential and uncertainty over the USMCA free trade deal.

Data showed the region's second largest economy grew more than expected in August from the prior month, with all three main sectors posting gains, official data showed.

Elsewhere, Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes, with a notably thin presence of security forces.

The country's legacy international maturities were marginally higher.

Meanwhile, US first lady Melania Trump secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said.

Kyiv's hard currency bonds (XS2895057334=TE), (XS2895056369=TE) gained over a cent following the news.

data.title: Genmab Announces Rinatabart Sesutecan (Rina-S®) Demonstrates Statistically Significant Improvement in Progression-Free Survival and Overall Survival in Patients with Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer
data.description:
Company Announcement

COPENHAGEN, Denmark; October 23, 2026

  • Phase 3 RAINFOL™-02 trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) and its key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS) with rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S®) compared to investigator’s choice chemotherapy
  • Results demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS and OS in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC)
  • Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting and discussed with regulatory authorities worldwide

Genmab A/S announced today positive topline results from the global Phase 3 RAINFOL™-02 trial of rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S®), an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeted, topoisomerase I (TOPO1)-inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) regardless of FRα expression level or prior treatment with mirvetuximab. The trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS), with Rina-S demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement compared with investigator’s choice chemotherapy in the intent-to-treat (ITT) and in the primary analysis set (PAS) populations.

The ITT population (N=584) comprised of all randomized patients with PROC, regardless of FRα expression. The PAS population (N=492) mandated patients with FRα expression ≥75% PS2+ to have been treated with mirvetuximab.

In the ITT population, Rina-S demonstrated a 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.29; 95% CI, 0.23-0.37; p<0.0001). In the PAS population, Rina-S demonstrated a 67% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.33; 95% CI, 0.26–0.42; p<0.0001).

The study also met its key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS), demonstrating a statically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in the ITT population (HR 0.43; 95% CI, 0.31–0.59; p<0.0001) and in the PAS population (HR 0.44; 95% CI, 0.31–0.63; p<0.0001).

The observed safety profile was consistent with the known profile of Rina-S, with no new safety signals or unexpected safety concerns identified.

“As the first Phase 3 readout from our Rina-S program, the positive topline results from RAINFOL-02 mark a significant milestone for Genmab and strengthen our confidence in Rina-S’s potential for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. These results advance our ambition to become a leader in gynecologic oncology and reflect our commitment to improving the lives of patients with high unmet medical needs,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab. “We look forward to discussing these results and potential next steps with regulatory authorities worldwide. We are deeply grateful to the patients, caregivers, and investigators whose participation made this study possible.”

Based on these results, Genmab plans to engage with regulatory authorities worldwide regarding potential next steps. The data will also be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting.

“Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer remains one of the greatest challenges in gynecologic oncology, with patients often facing a poor prognosis and limited effective treatment options. The Phase 3 RAINFOL-02 results set a new benchmark in addressing this urgent unmet need regardless of FRα expression,” said Angeles Alvarez Secord, MD, MHSc, the study’s lead investigator for the Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) and Professor of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the Duke Cancer Institute. “The 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression and 57% reduction in the risk of death underscore the potential of Rina-S to change clinical practice if approved by offering a therapeutic option for a broad patient population.”

Rina-S is being evaluated in a broad clinical development program spanning multiple gynecologic cancers and other solid tumors. The program includes five Phase 3 trials evaluating Rina-S in PROC (RAINFOL-02; NCT06619236), recurrent or progressive endometrial cancer (RAINFOL-03; NCT07166094), platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC) maintenance therapy (RAINFOL-04; NCT07225270), second-line PSOC (RAINFOL-07; NCT07564141), and in first-line ovarian cancer as maintenance therapy (RAINFOL-10; NCT07859215). Additional studies include the Phase 1/2 RAINFOL-01 trial (NCT05579366) and Phase 2 trials in non-small cell lung cancer (RAINFOL-05; NCT07288177) and advanced gastrointestinal cancers (RAINFOL-09; NCT07539311).

On Wednesday, October 28 at 5:00 p.m. CET/12:00 p.m. EDT, Genmab will host an investor update. To register, visit genmab.com/events-presentations.

About the RAINFOL-02 Trial

RAINFOL-02 (NCT06619236) is a randomized, open-label, multicenter Phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of Rina-S versus investigator’s choice chemotherapy in 582 patients with PROC regardless of FRα expression level. Patients are randomized 1:1 to receive either Rina-S 120 mg/m² on Day 1 of each three-week treatment cycle or one of four standard-of-care chemotherapy agents: paclitaxel, topotecan, PLD, or gemcitabine. The primary endpoint is investigator-assessed PFS. Key secondary endpoints are OS and objective response rate (ORR). Other secondary endpoints include PFS by blinded independent central review, duration of response, incidence of adverse events and laboratory abnormalities, time from randomization to second disease progression or death, and change from baseline in global health status/quality of life. Efficacy is evaluated in two populations. The ITT population (N = 584) includes all randomized patients, regardless of FRα expression level. The PAS (N=492), a subset of the ITT population, includes only patients with FRα expression <75% PS2+ and patients previously treated with mirvetuximab if eligible based on FRα expression ≥75% PS2+ and available in the region.

About Ovarian Cancer

Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major global health issue, more than 320,000 new cases diagnosed annually worldwide.i It ranks as the eighth most common cancer and the eighth leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women globally.ii The disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage because its symptoms, including abdominal bloating, pelvic pain and difficulty eating, can be subtle and nonspecific.iii Approximately 70-90% of women with advanced-stage OC worldwide experience a recurrence after initial treatment.iv OC has a low five-year survival rate, which varies significantly by region, but generally hovers around 30-50%.v,vi

About Rinatabart Sesutecan (Rina-S; GEN1184)

Rina-S (GEN1184) is an investigational ADC. It is composed of a novel human monoclonal antibody directed at FRα, a hydrophilic protease-cleavable linker, and exatecan, a TOPO1 inhibitor payload. The clinical trial program for Rina-S continues to expand, including ovarian, endometrial, and other cancers with unmet need.

The safety and efficacy of Rina-S have not been established. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, ADCs, immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. Genmab’s science powers eight approved antibody medicines, and the company is advancing a strong late-stage clinical pipeline, including wholly owned programs, with the goal of delivering transformative medicines to patients.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

data.title: American Express to Cut 5% of Global Workforce — 3rd Update
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

American Express plans to cut about 5% of its global workforce, a move the company said is aimed at reducing layers and speeding up decision making.

The layoff plans came as the credit-card company reported higher third-quarter profit and revenue as its customers continue to spend more. The results prompted the company to raise its profit outlook for the year.

The stock declined 3.3% to $314.57 on Friday. Shares are down 15% this year.

The job cuts will affect roughly 3,500 roles, American Express said.

Chief Executive Stephen Squeri said the move aims to streamline the company's teams to align on key focus areas, boost efficiency and invest further in its priorities, like adding more perks for its cardmembers.

"We've got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over the next few years, we needed to become a more agile and efficient organization," Squeri said during a call with analysts.

American Express now forecasts earnings per share of $18.30 to $18.60 for the full year, up from $17.30 to $17.90 previously. The new outlook factors in a boost from the sale of the company's equity investment in Global Business Travel Group, part of which it is reinvesting in the restructuring plan.

The company expects adjusted earnings per share--which exclude the effects of the sale and restructuring--of $17.60 to $17.90, and said it remains on track for sales growth of 10% this year.

Analysts polled by FactSet project earnings of $17.61 a share on revenue growth of 10% for the year.

Squeri attributed the guidance raise to the company's performance so far this year.

American Express, which targets higher-income consumers, is seeing strength in billings as it acquires new customers and retains its existing card members, he said, and as it continues to improve its membership model.

The company has been investing further in its roster of membership credit cards that come with annual fees and a range of perks. For instance its Platinum card, which was refreshed last year, comes with access to premium travel perks like airport lounges and luxury hotel benefits.

Going forward, Squeri said American Express aims to improve the customer experience with the help of artificial intelligence. For example, the company is looking to use the technology to offer customers more personalized experiences in areas like its restaurant partnerships, which give certain cardmembers access to sought-after reservations and other perks.

"AI gives us the opportunity to take our value propositions much further," Squeri said.

Third-quarter profit was $3.71 billion, or $5.42 a share, compared with $2.9 billion, or $4.14 a share, a year earlier.

Adjusted earnings per share were $4.68, compared with analyst estimates of $4.48, according to FactSet.

Revenue net of interest expense rose 9% to $20.06 billion. Analysts forecast revenue of $20.12 billion.

The increase in sales was primarily due to higher card-member spending, higher net interest income on growth in card balances, and card fee growth, American Express said.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

data.title: Analysts weigh in on Moderna's big drop following cancer vaccine results
data.description:
Moderna closed Thursday down ~17% after phase 3 data was leaked on the company's personalized cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene, and the Street is offering theories on why.

That data showed that intismeran autogene plus Merck's Keytruda (pembrolizumab) cut the risk of melanoma returning or death by 42% vs. Keytruda alone, meeting the primary endpoint. The risk of distant metastasis or death, the secondary endpoint, was reduced by 38% compared to Keytruda alone.

One analyst said that the data wasn't as robust as in phase 2. Another stated that the combination could become the standard of care. And a third questioned whether it would become a transformative oncology therapy.

RBC Capital Markets' Lucca Issi, who has a sector perform on shares, noted that phase 2 data for recurrent free survival and distance metastasis free survival were, respectively, 49% and 59%.

Although the phase 2 trial enrolled an earlier cancer stage population compared to phase 3, "Nonetheless, if you look at the [intent-to-treat population] (which is the way the FDA looks at it), the HRs are numerically inferior vs Phase II....Overall, this is not the first time that we have seen impressive Phase II being followed by a more muted benefit in Phase III, but we do believe that this can't be confidence boosting..."

Piper Sandler's Edward Tenthof, who rates Moderna at overweight, said that Thursday's selloff was due to concerns that the standard of care will be neoadjuvant Keytruda. It is important to note that Keytruda has yet to be approved in this setting for melanoma.

"We believe the INTerpath-001 trial appropriately compared againstcurrent SOC and that approval in adjuvant melanoma would be an advantageous label and lead to clinical uptake," he wrote.

Citi's Geoff Meacham provided 10 reasons why, following the data, he doesn't like Moderna's risk/reward. Among them are that positive results do not mean a transformative modality change in treatment, it does not establish an "effective cure," and Moderna's valuation requires more than just the trial results.

"We agree that intismeran looks approvable in adjuvant melanoma, but the bigger picture is that it adds tumor sequencing, manufacturing lead time, treatment coordination and high cost to an already approved and highly effective anti-PD-1 backbone," Meacham wrote.

data.title: KLM cancels dozens of flights due to strong winds, spokesperson says
data.description:
Airline KLM, the Dutch arm of Air France KLM , cancelled 20 flights on Friday due to strong winds in the Netherlands caused by Storm Austen, with a further 22 cancellations expected on Saturday, a spokesperson said.

  • The Dutch weather service (KNMI) warned that heavy wind gusts of 75 to 90 km per hour were expected in several parts of the country on Friday and throughout the weekend

  • Schiphol airport, one of Europe's busiest hubs, told Dutch news agency ANP that it was experiencing little disruption from the weather conditions, with no other airlines cancelling flights for the same reason

  • Storm Austen disrupted power supplies and transport across several European countries on Friday, leaving nearly 300,000 French homes and 12,000 British homes without electricity amid strong winds and heavy rain

data.title: Kansas City Fed Services Activity Index Rises in October
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Services activity in the middle of the U.S. rose in October, while expectations for future activity moved lower, according to a monthly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

The Tenth District Services Survey's composite index, a weighted average of indexes covering revenue/sales, employment and inventory, came in at 10 in October, compared with readings of 0 in September and minus 3 in August. Readings above zero indicate expansion, while those below zero indicate contraction.

The Kansas City Fed said business services cooled slightly this month, driven by moderate declines in activity in the transportation sector, while consumer services ticked up, led by increased activity in health services and non-discretionary retail trade.

The bank said its index of expectations for future services activity came in at 4 in October, down from 12 in September, amid lower employment expectations.

The Kansas City Fed's survey, released Friday, includes participants from such service industries as retail and wholesale trade, automobile dealers, real estate and restaurants. The survey provides information on current services activity in the Tenth District, which includes Colorado, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, the northern half of New Mexico and the western third of Missouri.

The bank's monthly manufacturing survey, released Thursday, showed that manufacturing activity in the central U.S. expanded at a slower pace this month.

data.title: BeOne Medicines Says Esophageal Cancer Treatments Had Higher Survival Rates in Phase 3 Study
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

BeOne Medicines said a new combined treatment for esophageal cancer demonstrated an improved overall survival rate in a Phase 3 study.

The oncology company said patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who took a combination of Tevimbra and Ziihera, along with chemotherapy, had an overall survival rate of nearly 40% after three years. The median overall survival was 27 months, the company said.

The result was a "sustained" improvement compared with a combination of chemotherapy and trastuzumab, BeOne said.

The company also tested Ziihera and chemotherapy without the addition of Tevimbra. Patients on that regimen had an overall survival rate of 22.9 months, BeOne said, adding that the result was a significant improvement over the control and met the study's primary endpoint.

The company said the additional four months of median survival when adding Tevimbra did not reach statistical significance in the context of an underpowered analysis.

"Following the U.S. approval in August, these longer-term data provide further evidence supporting Tevimbra plus Ziihera and chemotherapy as the new standard of care in all first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma patients, regardless of PD-L1 status," said Mark Lanasa, BeOne's chief medical officer, solid tumors.

Shares of BeOne were down 2% to $374.57 as of late Friday morning.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Trump Called Musk and Asked Him to Lift Ukraine Starlink Restrictions — WSJ
data.description:
By Alexander Ward and Lara Seligman

WASHINGTON — President Trump called Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to lift restrictions on a military-grade version of Starlink in Ukraine that the SpaceX chief had throttled, U.S. officials said.

Some U.S. and Ukrainian officials said the system was working more normally on Thursday, after Trump and Musk spoke, but wasn't restored to full functionality. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Friday "the speed has not been restored."

Trump told Musk in their call that he was frustrated the system's speeds remained capped at around 100 miles an hour, officials said. The speed limit rendered some of Ukraine's offensive drones and interceptors powerless against Russian attacks. Their conversation followed a Wall Street Journal report revealing that Musk ordered the slowdown, though SpaceX and the White House have differing accounts about whether the world's richest man acted alone or at the administration's behest.

Trump has told aides and allies this week that he wanted to reverse the slowdown of Starlink, which Ukraine's forces use to defend themselves along the front line, the officials said.

"Removal of the throttle limit will do much to enable Ukraine's strike capabilities at operational depths and its current effort to scale up deployment of jet-powered interceptors," said Michael Kofman, an expert on the war at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Kofman added that he had heard from Ukrainian military units that early tests suggest the system is now working more regularly.

"I don't comment one way or the other," Trump said on Thursday when asked about the Journal's reporting that he had called Musk. "The bottom line: He put it back."

A Ukrainian official said some military units had experienced higher Starlink speeds while others were facing the same cap. "We keep waiting for the information and clarification from the American side about the situation. There is no response yet."

Musk and SpaceX didn't respond to requests for comment.

The White House referred the Journal to Trump's recent denials that he had asked Musk to throttle Starlink's speeds or knew who issued the order. Trump and Musk spoke about Ukraine and Starlink on the day the slowdown became public, the Journal previously reported.

The president and his top officials have spent a week facing questions about why Starlink was throttled and whether they ordered it. The slowdown began days after Trump and Musk both publicly criticized Zelensky for attacking Russian diesel refineries, which Trump blames for elevated energy prices. Trump has repeatedly denied giving the order or knowing who did.

The connectivity issues helped sink U.S.-Ukraine relations to their lowest level in months.

Asked about Musk's decision to throttle Starlink, Vice President JD Vance on Thursday told reporters that "it's completely understandable that he doesn't want to get in the middle of a war without the U.S. government effectively directing him on what to do."

"I don't think this is about Elon. I think it's fundamentally about what America's policy in Ukraine and Russia is going to be," he said.

His message differed from comments by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Musk had the authority to enforce his company's terms of service without input from the administration.

"There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied to, and that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions," Hegseth said, speaking to reporters earlier this week.

The speed cap meant Ukrainian hardware couldn't stay connected to the satellite-based network when traveling at high rates of speed, according to people familiar with the matter. Ukrainian officials said the move would cost Ukrainian lives.

Russia overnight launched another massive barrage against Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, just a day after Moscow said it had agreed to trilateral talks with the U.S. and Ukraine to end the war.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D., Conn.) on Thursday announced an investigation into how Starlink was degraded for Ukraine without notice and the implications of the Pentagon's dependence on SpaceX for critical satellite communications.

Write to Alexander Ward at alex.ward@wsj.com and Lara Seligman at lara.seligman@wsj.com

data.title: NYMEX Overview: Petroleum Futures Rise For Second Day as Mideast Tensions Remain High — OPIS
data.description:
Crude oil and refined product futures prices were seeing a second day of solid increases Friday as escalating tensions in the Middle East had most contracts ending the week with gains.

U.S. crude prices were back above the $100/bbl mark at 11:15 a.m. ET, with the December West Texas Intermediate crude contract trading $2.81 higher to $102.28/bbl, a change of 2.8%.

January WTI prices were up by $2.76 to $100.28/bbl.

Brent crude prices were seeing similar proportional increases, with December Brent rising by $3.03 to $116.20/bbl and the January contract ahead by $2.68 to $111.34/bbl.

RBOB futures were leading products higher, with the November contract ahead by 4.15cts to $3.2180/gal, a gain of 1.4%. December prices were rising by 4.48cts to $3.1341/gal.

ULSD increases were under 0.5%, with the November contract moving up by 2.72cts to $4.9593/gal and December prices rising by 2.7cts to $4.7636/gal.

The gains come as tensions continue to increase in the Persian Gulf region, with the U.S. and Israel reportedly preparing to resume strikes on Iran and Iranian leaders threatening to retaliate by striking civilian targets in the region.

"The physical market is more balanced than the headlines suggest. Gulf oil exports have recovered significantly in recent weeks, which gives the market some protection, while emergency stock releases have also helped ease immediate supply fears," said Zaheer Anwari, founder of The Revacy Fund, in an analysis Friday. "That does not remove the risk. Shipping through the region remains disrupted, freight and insurance costs are still elevated and any fresh attack on energy infrastructure could quickly tighten supply again."

data.title: Comfort Systems Stock Plunges After Strong Earnings. Why Wall Street Isn't Buying It. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Comfort Systems USA delivered another quarter of blockbuster earnings, but that wasn't enough to buoy shares of the HVAC and electrical company.

Instead, Comfort Systems stock plunged 12% to $1,129.93 on Friday, putting it on pace toward its largest daily percent decrease since January 2025 and placing it among the worst performers in the S&P 500 for the session, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Shares have stumbled 32% in October, but remain up 21% for the year.

On Thursday, the company reported adjusted earnings of $13.91 a share for its third quarter on Thursday, exceeding Wall Street's projection for $12.85 a share, according to FactSet. Revenue surged 54% year over year to $3.7 billion, topping consensus expectations of $3.4 billion.

CEO Brian Lane described the results as "extraordinary" in an earnings release, citing "relentless demand." He pointed to Comfort Systems' backlog nearly doubling to $17.81 billion, compared with $9.3 billion a year ago.

Comfort Systems has emerged as an unlikely winner of the broader artificial-intelligence buildout, with shares outpacing even the likes of Nvidia in recent years. The company supplies the cooling and electrical infrastructure needed to keep power-hungry data centers running.

Still, signs of pressure on Comfort Systems' profit margins might have raised red flags about whether the company can sustain its rapid growth. More broadly, investors have been questioning whether the AI spending boom can maintain its red-hot pace, and AI-related stocks have taken a hit as a result.

Gross margin narrowed to 24.8% in the third quarter amid rising labor expenses, down from 25.9% in the prior quarter, though it was unchanged year over year. Operating margin slipped to 16.6% from 17.1% sequentially, but improved from 15.5% from the year-ago period.

Goldman Sachs has also questioned the sustainability of the AI spending boom that has fueled Comfort Systems' growth.

In a note earlier this week, Goldman analysts lowered their price target for Comfort Systems stock to $1,875 from $2,159 while maintaining a Buy rating. They noted that valuations across construction and engineering stocks have fallen 14% since second-quarter earnings, as investors question whether tech companies can withstand their massive data-center spending beyond 2027.

Growing legislative scrutiny of data-center development could also pose headwinds for companies exposed to the industry, the analysts said.

data.title: South Africa to allow fund managers 100% foreign assets under new framework
data.description:
By Colleen Goko

South African fund managers will be able to hold 100% of portfolios in foreign assets under ring-fenced mandates, regulators said on Friday, in a new framework that exempts qualifying vehicles from a longstanding 45% offshore investment cap.

The South African Reserve Bank, National Treasury and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange briefed investors on the draft Synthetic Financial Centre (SFC) framework, published on Wednesday, which would allow licensed asset managers, banks, insurers and private equity firms to manage global portfolios in any currency from a South African base.

The 45% limit would still apply when an institution commits capital to an SFC vehicle. But once the funds are inside a registered mandate, the manager could invest them entirely offshore. The originating institution would still count the investment towards its own prudential foreign limit.

Stuart Theobald, executive chairperson of Krutham, a think tank, and convenor of Operation Phumelela, a private sector initiative led by the JSE to boost the competitiveness of South Africa's financial sector, called the lifting of the cap "the most fundamental change" in the framework.

Close to 5 trillion rand ($301 billion) in South African portfolio assets are held offshore, much of it routed through overseas centres because local rules have made it difficult to manage fully global portfolios from Johannesburg.

"The SFC really positions South Africa with a framework that makes it competitive," JSE CEO Valdene Reddy said.

The framework is part of a sweeping overhaul of South Africa's decades-old exchange controls that the JSE estimates could attract 10 trillion rand in investment over time.

Olano Makhubela, head of the SARB's Financial Surveillance Department, said the 45% prudential limit would remain a "long-term feature" of South Africa's capital-flow framework.

Vukile Davidson, chief director of financial markets and stability at National Treasury, said a second phase could consider tax alignment and could allow foreign-currency listings on South African exchanges. The draft is open for public comment until November 30.

($1 = 16.5875 rand)

data.title: Gold set for steep weekly loss as rising oil prices bolster Fed rate hike bets
data.description:
Key points:
  • Spot gold hits lowest level since July
  • Brent crude hits more than five-month high
  • Fed interest-rate decision, US PCE data due next week
  • India gold demand strengthens on lower prices, festive purchases

By Noel John and Anushree Mukherjee

Gold fell to a three-month low on Friday, and was headed for its steepest weekly decline in over four months as higher energy prices fueled inflation concerns and reinforced elevated US rate expectations ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting.

Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,000.59 an ounce by 11:20 a.m. EDT (1520 GMT), after earlier slipping below the $4,000 mark for the first time since mid-July and touching a session low of $3,975.23.

Bullion has fallen 4% so far this week, putting it on track for its worst week since June.

US gold futures for December delivery fell 1.1% to $4,014.60 per ounce.

Brent crude touched a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies.

"Heightened inflation concerns suggest that major central banks of the world won't be able to ease monetary policies as quickly as they want to. All that's working against the gold and silver market bulls at present," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange.

The selloff in technology stocks has also led to margin calls for equity traders and investors, prompting them to sell gold and silver assets, Wyckoff added.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq touched their lowest in five weeks on Friday as caution prevailed after a sharp selloff in AI-linked stocks.

Meanwhile, traders largely expect the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, although stronger-than-expected US consumer and producer inflation data released last week bolstered the case for tighter monetary policy later this year.

They see a 92% chance of the Fed leaving rates unchanged next week and an 83% probability of a December hike, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

The US Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, on October 29 could offer further insight.

Elsewhere, gold buying picked up in India this week as lower prices during the major Dussehra festival boosted purchases and lifted premiums, while physical demand in top consumer China was steady even as cautious consumers continued to curb jewellery spending. [GOL/AS]

Among other metals, spot silver slid 0.7% to $54.17 per ounce, and palladium dropped 0.5% to $1,053.11, hitting their lowest since November 2025 and June 2025 respectively. Spot platinum fell 0.5% to $1,562.11 per ounce, its lowest since July.

All three metals were headed for weekly declines.

data.title: Booz Allen slides on Q2 revenue miss, hurt by civil division

data.title: ECB Will Need to Reassure Markets on France Concerns at Next Meeting — Market Talk
